issues.legal_issue: In a proceeding to declare property evacuee property, the Custodian need not conduct a general inquiry into interested persons before issuing notice and may act on the information available to him.
material_facts: Village records showed the names of two persons as mortgagees of the agricultural property.
The Custodian treated those recorded mortgagees as persons interested and issued notice to them at an address away from the village.
The Custodian had no information about whether the mortgagees were alive, and the notice could not be served because they had died before it was issued.
issues.conclusion: The Custodian was not required to make a general inquiry into all persons interested and complied with the requirement to issue notice on the basis of the information available to him. However, the notice was ineffective because its addressees were already dead.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7(1) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, the Custodian may form an opinion and issue notice to persons interested on the basis of available information; he is not expected to make a general inquiry into all interested persons. The Court followed Abdul Hakim Khan v. Regional Settlement Commissioner, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 531.

predicates.evacuee_property_declaration_proceeding: The proceeding sought a determination that property was evacuee property.
predicates.custodian_used_available_information: The Custodian identified persons to notify using information available to him, including property records.
predicates.no_information_addressees_were_dead: The Custodian had no information that the persons he notified had died.

issues.definition: When a property-declaration proceeding is based on available information and the Custodian lacks information that the notified persons have died, a general inquiry is not required.

issues.legal_issue: A declaration that property is evacuee property does not affect a mortgagee's rights where the evacuees held only the equity of redemption, so the absence of effective notice to the mortgagees does not invalidate the declaration as against those rights.
material_facts: The owners migrated to Pakistan and the Custodian declared them and the property evacuees.
The property was alleged to have been mortgaged to persons who had died before the notice was issued; their successors claimed the mortgagees' interests.
The declaration concerned the evacuees' interest in the mortgaged property, which was their equity of redemption, not the mortgagees' rights.
issues.conclusion: The notice to the deceased mortgagees was ineffective, but the declaration did not affect any mortgagee rights and the failure to notify the successors was of no consequence to those rights. The declaration vested only the evacuees' interest, leaving the property subject to any mortgagee rights.
issues.legal_principle: The evacuees' interest in mortgaged property consisted of the equity of redemption, and a declaration of that interest as evacuee property could not affect rights the evacuees did not own. The Court relied on section 7(1) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, and followed Abdul Hakim Khan v. Regional Settlement Commissioner, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 531.

predicates.evacuee_property_declaration_proceeding: The proceeding sought a declaration that property or an interest in it was evacuee property.
predicates.evacuees_held_only_redemption_interest: The evacuees' interest in the property was limited to the right to redeem it from a mortgage.
predicates.claimant_asserted_mortgage_rights: A claimant asserted rights as a mortgagee or successor to a mortgagee.

issues.definition: When a declaration proceeding concerns only the evacuees' redemption interest and a claimant asserts mortgage rights, the declaration leaves those mortgage rights unaffected.

issues.legal_issue: The Custodian may not take action against persons claiming a mortgage interest, or their occupants, before the evacuee and claimant interests in the composite property have been separated.
material_facts: The appellants claimed that their predecessors had held the property as mortgagees and that they or their tenants were in possession.
No action had been taken under the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951, to separate the evacuees' interest from the claimed mortgagee interest.
The Custodian held only the evacuees' interest, subject to any mortgagee rights.
issues.conclusion: Until proper separation proceedings are taken, the Custodian cannot take action against the appellants or their tenants who are said to be in possession of the property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10 of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 empowers the competent officer to separate evacuee interests from claimants' interests in composite property; the evacuee interest becomes free from encumbrances only after that separation. Until then, the Custodian's interest remains subject to the claimed mortgage rights.

rule.if: custodian_enforcement_proceeding and claimant_asserted_mortgage_rights and claimant_or_occupant_in_possession and interests_not_separated

predicates.custodian_enforcement_proceeding: The proceeding concerned action by the Custodian against persons claiming an interest in property or persons occupying it.
predicates.claimant_asserted_mortgage_rights: A claimant asserted rights in the property as a mortgagee or successor to a mortgagee.
predicates.claimant_or_occupant_in_possession: The claimant or the claimant's occupant was said to be in possession of the property.
predicates.interests_not_separated: The evacuee's interest and the claimant's interest had not been separated through the relevant process.

issues.definition: When the Custodian seeks to act against a mortgage claimant or an occupant in possession before the competing interests have been separated, the Custodian may not act against them.
